locator: The whole vignette: the house's street front from its south corner to its north corner, the north side wall to its rear corner, the mansard roof with its dormers and the taller crown over the north part, the hooded front bay, the stoop and porch, and the lattice front fence. The camera solve (data/reference_views/law_house_1620_prairie/landowner_1874_from_northeast.json) locates every feature read off it.

note: The only located view of 1620 in its own time, engraved two years after it was built (c. 1872). From across Prairie Avenue to the north-east it shows a Second Empire house of two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with round-headed dormers. The street front is light-toned (an engraving's light face, not a colour); its north 3.75 m (the part of Robinson 1886's L that runs the full depth) rises into a taller curved crown with one round-headed dormer and carries two round-headed windows a storey; the south part carries a one-storey bay window under a bracketed, flared hood, an upper window over it, and the entrance, reached by a stoop rising north to a balustraded porch. A bracketed cornice runs round the front and the north wall; the north wall shows two storeys of flat-headed windows and two mansard dormers and a tall stack at the front. A lattice fence of interlaced arches on a base stands on the street line, and a board fence on the north side. The camera is solved from the plan's corners with the K01 rectangle's lengths, so each height read off it is a measurement through that solve.
